ITQAN:v3p101/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p101/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p101/r2.claim: A thing may be named by what it used to be: adults are still called orphans, former spouses husbands, and a person a criminal for earlier worldly crimes.
ITQAN:v3p101/r2.anchor: الحادى عشر تسمية الشيء باسم ما كان عليه نحو ( وآتوا اليتامى أموالهم ) أي الذين كانوا يتامى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r1.claim: Islahi treats 20:74–76 as a divine insertion: their afterlife register suits God’s majesty, differs from the surrounding speech, and recalls an earlier insertion at 20:53–59.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r1.anchor: This verse and the two succeeding ones are from God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r2.claim: A wrongdoer here is someone disobedient to God who has not repented.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r2.anchor: The word “wrongdoer” in the translation refers to a person who is disobedient to God and did not have the courtesy to repent.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r3.claim: The phrase about neither dying nor living depicts punishment from which death offers no relief and no escape exists.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p51/r3.anchor: Death can alleviate the greatest of punishments.

SAMIN-DURR:20:74/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:74/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:74/r1.claim: The pronoun in إنه is a pronoun of the matter, and the conditional sentence is its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:20:74/r1.anchor: الهاء ضمير الشأن. والجملة الشرطية خبرها.

SAMIN-DURR:20:74/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:74/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:74/r2.claim: مجرما is a circumstantial accusative describing the subject of يأت.

SAMIN-DURR:20:74/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:74/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:74/r3.claim: The clause لا يموت may be a circumstantial clause referring to the pronoun in له or to جهنم, since either has a pronoun represented in it.
SAMIN-DURR:20:74/r3.anchor: يجوز أن يكون حالا من الهاء في " له " وأن يكون حالا من " جهنم "؛ لأن

ASAD-NOTES:20:74/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:74/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:74/r1.claim: A sinner who appears before God faces Hell, where he neither dies nor lives.
ASAD-NOTES:20:74/r1.anchor: VERILY, as for him who shall appear before his Sustainer [on Judgment Day] lost in sin - his [portion], behold, shall be hell

ASAD-NOTES:20:74#n58/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:74#n58/r1.speaker: Baghawi, Baydawi
ASAD-NOTES:20:74#n58/r1.claim: Baghawi and Baydawi explain that the condemned neither undergo spiritual rebirth nor find peace through extinction.
ASAD-NOTES:20:74#n58/r1.anchor: he will neither be reborn spiritually nor find peace through extinction (Baghawi, Baydawi)

ASAD-NOTES:20:74#n58/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:74#n58/r2.speaker: Baydawi
ASAD-NOTES:20:74#n58/r2.claim: Baydawi identifies the term mu'mim in this context with someone who consciously and persistently denied God during life, contrasting it with mu'min in the next verse.
ASAD-NOTES:20:74#n58/r2.anchor: the former term is here applied to one who, in his lifetime, has consciously and persistently denied God (Baydawi)

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234/r1.claim: The two conditional statements explain why God is better and more enduring, confirm that claim, and refute Pharaoh’s boast.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : ( إنه ( إلى آخر الشرطيتين تعليل من جهتهم لكونه تعالى شأنه خير وأبقى وتحقيق له وابطال لما ادعاه اللعين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234/r2.claim: The opening pronoun of شأن alerts the listener to the gravity of what follows and reinforces its force.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234/r2.anchor: وتصديرهما بضمير الشأن للتنبيه على فخامة مضمونها ولزيادة تقرير له

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234/r3.claim: The criminal is one who dies in unbelief and sins; hell ends neither in death that releases him nor in a life from which he benefits.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234/r3.anchor: أي قوله تعالى ( من يات ربه مجرما ( بأن مات الكفر والمعاصي + ( فان لهم جهنم لا يموت فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r8.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r8.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that a major sinner is a criminal—the root suggests cutting fruit, then came to mean committing something reprehensible—and every criminal is assigned hell, so the threat is certain.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#3/r8.anchor: استدل المعتزلة بالشرطية الأولى على القطع بعذاب مرتكب الكبيرة قالوا : مرتكب الكبيرة مجرم لأن اصل الجرم قطع الثمرة عن الشجرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r1.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r1.claim: Sunnis reject the premise that ‘criminal’ here includes a major sinner: the Qur’an often uses it for unbelievers, as in the people questioned about Saqar and those who mocked believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r1.anchor: واجاب أهل السنة بانا لا نسلم الصغرى لجواز أن يراد بالمجرم الكافر فكثيرا ما جاء في القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r2.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r2.claim: Even granting the first premise, they say the rule applies only absent forgiveness; they also deny that the conditional particle is certainly universal, so a categorical threat does not follow.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r2.anchor: وعلى تقدير تسليم هذه المقدمة لانسلم الكبرى على اطلاقها وإنما هي كلية بشرط عدم العفو مع انا لا نسلم أن من الشرطية قطعية في العموم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r4.speaker: أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r4.claim: They reject the intermediate station between faith and unbelief and argue that accountable people are either believers or unbelievers, so major sinners cannot be excluded from the promise on that basis.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p234#4/r4.anchor: فاذا قالوا : مرتكب الكبيرة على يقال له مؤمن كما لا يقال كافر لاثباتهم المنزلة بين المنزلتين فلا يدخل ذلك في العموم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري؛ رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r1.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports the Prophet distinguishing hell’s permanent inhabitants, who neither die nor live, from others whom the fire kills; intercessors then bring them in groups to the river of Life, where they grow anew like gourds. The report is cited from Muslim, Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh, without a grading.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r1.anchor: عن أبى سعيد الخدرى ان رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r2.claim: Some say a sinful believer who enters hell dies, unlike the unbelieving criminal; they take the fire’s killing literally and the verbal noun as emphasis against metaphor.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r2.anchor: ثم أن العاصي إذا دخل جهنم لا يكون حاله كحال المجرم الكافر إذا دخلها بل قيل : إنه يموت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r3.claim: They compare the emphatic verbal noun to the emphatic wording ‘God spoke to Moses directly.’
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r3.anchor: وجعل المصدر تاكيدا لدفع توهم المجاز كما قيل في قوله تعالى ( وكلم الله مو

ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r4.speaker: ذلك القائل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r4.claim: On this view, the believers remain in hell after dying until God wills, deprived of paradise during that period in addition to the pain of the fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r4.anchor: وذكر أن فائدة بقائهم في النار بعد امانتهم إلى حيث شاء الله تعالى حرمانهم من الجنة تلك المدة وذلك منضم إلى عذابهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r5.claim: Another view takes their death figuratively: the fire leaves them like the dead, without full awareness of its torment; a verbal noun can accompany figurative usage, as in saying someone was ‘killed’ with a beating.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن تميتهم مجاز والمراد انها تجعل حالهم قريبة من حال الموتى بأن لا يكون لهم شعور تام بالعذاب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r6.claim: The verbal noun cannot specify a kind of dying, since death has only one kind, the departure of the soul; causes vary, but death is one.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r6.anchor: ولا يصح أن يقال : المصدر لبيان النوع أي نميتهم نوعا من الاماتة لأن الاماتة لا انواع لها بل هي نوع واحد وهو ازهاق الروح

ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r7.speaker: المجسمة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r7.claim: The anthropomorphists infer from ‘comes to his Lord’ that God has a location; the answer is that it means coming to the place of God’s promise or something similar.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p235/r7.anchor: واستدل المجسمة بقول سبحانه ( إنه من يأت ربه على ثبوت مكان له تعالى شأنه وأجيب بأن المراد من إتيانه تعالى إتيان موضع وعده عز وجل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r1.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r1.claim: One view treats the warning about a criminal as the beginning of God's speech.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r1.anchor: قيل: هذا ابتداء كلام من الله تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r2.claim: Another view makes it the sorcerers' continuation; a criminal is a polytheist who died in polytheism.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r2.anchor: وقيل: من تمام قول السحرة {مجرما} أي: مشركا، يعني: مات على الشرك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r3.claim: He does not die and thereby rest, nor live a life that brings benefit.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p286/r3.anchor: لا يموت فيها} فيستريح، {ولا يحيا} حياة ينتفع بها

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:74/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:74/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:74/r1.claim: The pronoun in innahu refers to the affair or matter.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:74/r1.anchor: { إنه } إن الأمر. { من يأت ربه

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:74/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:74/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:74/r2.claim: The criminal is one who dies persisting in disbelief and disobedience.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:74/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:74/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:74/r3.claim: He does not die and so cannot find relief.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:74/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:74/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:74/r4.claim: He has no comfortable or pleasant life.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r1.claim: A criminal is one who breaks what God commanded him to uphold; he faces Hell, the abode of humiliation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r1.anchor: أي قاطعا ما أمره به أن يوصل { فإن له جهنم } دار الإهانة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r2.claim: The sinner never dies despite the severity of Hell; Pharaoh's punishment, by contrast, would either kill quickly if severe or end in death if mild.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r2.anchor: لا يموت فيها } أبدا مع شدة عذابها . بخلاف عذابك الذي إن اشتد أمات فزال سريعا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r3.claim: The condemned person has no life in Hell from which he can benefit.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p32/r3.anchor: ولا يحيى * } فيها حياة ينتفع بها

DURR-FULL:v5p587/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p587/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p587/r3.claim: The Prophet distinguishes permanent Hell-dwellers, who neither die nor live, from others whom the fire kills; intercessors then bring them to the river of Life, where they regrow like floodborne cucumbers.
DURR-FULL:v5p587/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطب فأتى على هذه الآية {إنه من يأت ربه مجرما فإن له جهنم لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى} فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أما أهلها الذين هم أهلها

BURSEVI:v5p313/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p313/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p313/r1.claim: The opening means it is the case, and the statement explains why God is better and more enduring than Pharaoh.
BURSEVI:v5p313/r1.anchor: أي : الشأن وهو تعليل من جهتهم لكونه تعالى خيرا وأبقى

BURSEVI:v5p313/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p313/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p313/r2.claim: A criminal here is someone deeply immersed in wrongdoing who dies persisting in disbelief and sins, in contrast to the believer mentioned next.
BURSEVI:v5p313/r2.anchor: حال كونه متوغلا في إجرامه منهمكا فيه بأن يموت على الكفر والمعاصي ولأنه مذكور في مقابلة المؤمن

BURSEVI:v5p313/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p313/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p313/r3.claim: The condemned person does not die and so cannot reach the end of punishment or find relief, confirming that this punishment endures.
BURSEVI:v5p313/r3.anchor: فينتهي عذابه ويستريح وهذا تحقيق لكون عذابه أبقى

BURSEVI:v5p313/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p313/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p313/r4.claim: The person in Hell does not live a life from which he can benefit.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r1.claim: The warning about the criminal and the reward for believers interrupts the magicians’ story before the exodus account, serving as admonition and confirmation of the believers’ words.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r1.anchor: هذه الجمل معترضة بين حكاية قصة السحرة وبين ذكر قصة خروج بني إسرائيل ، ساقها الله موعظة وتأييدا لمقالة المؤمنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r2.claim: An alternative says the warning is spoken by Pharaoh’s believing magicians, but Ibn ʿĀshūr finds that unlikely because their speech is not similarly narrated elsewhere in parallel versions of the story.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r2.anchor: وقيل : هي من كلام أولئك المؤمنين . ويبعده أنه لم يحك نظيره عنهم في نظائر هذه القصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r3.claim: A مجرم is someone who commits a crime, meaning sin and a vile deed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r3.anchor: والمجرم : فاعل الجريمة ، وهي المعصية والفعل الخبيث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r4.claim: In Quranic usage, مجرم refers to an unbeliever, as in the verse about those who mocked believers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r4.anchor: والمجرم في اصطلاح القرآن هو الكافر ، كقوله تعالى : { إن الذين أجرموا كانوا من الذين آمنوا يضحكون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r5.claim: The lām in له marks deservedness: the criminal will inevitably end up in Hell.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r5.anchor: واللام في { له جهنم } لام الاستحقاق ، أي هو صائر إليها لا محالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r6.claim: The criminal’s punishment continues: he is not dead because he feels the torment, yet is not truly alive because such suffering is worse than death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r6.anchor: ويكون عذابه متجددا فيها ؛ فلا هو ميت لأنه يحس بالعذاب ولا هو حي لأنه في حالة الموت أهون منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r7.claim: The negated life is specifically a life free from torment and pain, so its denial does not conflict with the denial of death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r7.anchor: فالحياة المنفية حياة خاصة وهي الحياة الخالصة من العذاب والآلام . وبذلك لم يتناقض نفيها مع نفي الموت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r8.speaker: عباس بن مرداس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r8.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr adduces ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās’s verse about neither receiving nor preventing anything in war as a parallel formulation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r8.anchor: وهو كقول عباس بن مرداس : وقد كنت في الحرب ذا تدرإ فلم أعط شيئا ولم أمنع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r9.claim: This construction differs from expressions that negate both ends of a simple contrast, such as neither old nor young for the cow or neither eastern nor western for the olive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r9.anchor: وليس هذا من قبيل قوله { إنها بقرة لا فارض ولا بكر } ( البقرة : 68 ) ولا قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r10.claim: The verse excludes sinful believers from the eternally punished class; other evidence establishes the unbeliever’s eternity but not the sinful believer’s, a doctrine disputed with the Muʿtazilites and Kharijites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p268/r10.anchor: وأما خلود غير الكافرين في النار من أهل الكبائر فإن قوله { لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى } جعلها غير مشمولة لهذه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r1.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r1.claim: One group says these verses are the sorcerers' admonition to Pharaoh, explaining their choice.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r1.anchor: قالت فرقة هذه الآية بجملتها من كلام السحرة لفرعون على جهة الموعظة له والبيان فيما فعلوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r2.claim: Another says God addresses Muhammad here to show Pharaoh's evil, the sorcerers' virtue, and a warning through the story.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r2.anchor: وقالت فرقة بل هي من كلام الله تعالى لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم تنبيها على قبح ما فعل فرعون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r3.claim: A criminal is one who has acquired sins and offenses.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r4.claim: This describes unbelievers: torment brings them near death but does not finish them; their skins and punishment are renewed, so they do not live well.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r4.anchor: مختص بالكافر فإنه معذب عذابا ينتهي به إلى الموت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r5.claim: Sinful believers remain in distress near death until intercession releases them, but are neither killed nor given renewed punishment; this distinguishes them from unbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r5.anchor: فهم قبل أن تخرجهم الشفاعة في غمرة قد قاربوا الموت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r6.speaker: الحديث الصحيح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r6.claim: An authentic hadith says they are made to die a death; Ibn Atiyya explains this as meaning no one dies in the afterlife.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p53#2/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح «أنهم يماتون إماتة» وهذا هو معناه لأنه لا يموت في الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309/r1.claim: Here a criminal means a polytheist.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى إنه من يأت ربه مجرما يعني مشركا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309/r2.claim: The damned person neither dies and rests nor lives a life that benefits him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309/r2.anchor: لا يموت فيها فيستريح ولا يحيى حياة تنفعه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari cites a poem depicting misery as neither ending in death nor becoming a fully tasted life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p309/r3.anchor: أنشد ابن الأنباري في مثل هذا المعنى قوله ألا من لنفس لا تموت فينقضي شقاها ولا تحيا حياة لها طعم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir takes this as the magicians' continued warning to Pharaoh about God's everlasting punishment and their encouragement toward eternal reward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r1.anchor: الظاهر من السياق أن هذا من تمام ما وعظ به السحرة لفرعون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r2.claim: A criminal who meets God on Judgment Day enters Hell, where he neither dies nor lives.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r2.anchor: أي: يلقى الله يوم القيامة وهو مجرم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir links this description to verses saying Hell's punishment is not ended by death or lightened, and its inhabitants plead to die but are told they will remain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r3.anchor: كقوله: {لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا ولا يخفف عنهم من عذابها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r4.claim: The Prophet says those destined to remain in Hell neither die nor live; sinful people are burned to charcoal, then intercessors bring them in groups to Paradise's rivers, where they sprout like flood-carried seeds. Ahmad transmits it and Muslim includes it in his Sahih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "أما أهل النار الذين هم أهلها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r5.claim: A second report says the Prophet cited this verse in a sermon: those destined for Hell never die, while others are touched by the fire, then intercessors bring them to the river of Life, where they grow like cucumbers in a flood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p305#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي سعيد؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطب فأتى على هذه الآية

JISHUMI:v7p4702/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r5.claim: The statement about whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal may be God’s own parenthetical speech rather than part of the magicians’ reply, or it may remain their speech.
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r5.anchor: قيل: إنه خبر من الله اعترض بين القصة على غير وجه الحكاية، وقيل: هو حكاية عن السحرة

JISHUMI:v7p4702/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r6.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r6.claim: Abu Ali takes coming to one’s Lord as reaching the place God promised, namely the afterlife.
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r6.anchor: ومعجز إنه من يأت ربه قيل: إلى الموضع الذي وعده ربه، عن أبي علي. وهو الآخرة

JISHUMI:v7p4702/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r7.claim: Criminal here is explained either as a polytheist or as a sinner.

JISHUMI:v7p4702/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r8.claim: Hell is his dwelling: he neither dies and rests nor enjoys a good life.
JISHUMI:v7p4702/r8.anchor: فإن له جهنم أي: مأواه ومنزله جهنم لا يموت فيها فيستريح ولا يحيا حياة هنية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r7.claim: The three preceding verses are either a quotation of the magicians' speech or God's account rather than a quotation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p78/r7.anchor: قيل في هذه الآيات الثلاث : هي حكاية قولهم . وقيل : خبر من الله لا على وجه الحكاية

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p415/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p415/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p415/r1.claim: The damned neither benefit from life nor find relief in death, as a poet describes a soul that neither dies nor lives a life with any taste.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p415/r1.anchor: لا ينتفع بحياته ولا يستريح بموته , كما قال الشاعر : ألا من لنفس لا تموت فينقضي … شقاها ولا تحيا حياة لها طعم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p415/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p415/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p415/r2.claim: Alternatively, the disbeliever's soul remains caught in the throat: it does not depart in death or settle into life.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p415/r2.anchor: أن نفس الكافر معلقة بحنجرته كما أخبر الله عنه فلا يموت بفراقها . ولا يحيا باستقرارها

MUQATIL:20:74-76/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:74-76/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:74-76/r1.claim: A criminal here is a polytheist in the Hereafter; Muqatil addresses Pharaoh as such.

MUQATIL:20:74-76/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:74-76/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:74-76/r2.claim: The damned neither die and find relief nor live in a way that benefits them; Muqatil cites 87:1 as a parallel.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#2/r1.claim: Innahu contains the pronoun of the matter.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#2/r2.claim: Here a criminal means an unbeliever; lahu refers to that criminal.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#2/r3.claim: He does not die and gain relief through death, nor live a life from which he can benefit.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p62#2/r3.anchor: فيستربح بالموت ﴿ ولا يحيى ﴾ حياة ينتفع بها

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r9.claim: Some take the statement about the criminal as a continuation of what the magicians said after believing.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r9.anchor: قيل: هو من قول السحرة لما آمنوا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r10.claim: Others take it as a new divine statement.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r10.anchor: وقيل: ابتداء كلام من الله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r11.claim: The pronoun may refer to the matter or affair; Arabic can also omit إنه before the clause, as in the cited verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r11.anchor: والكناية في «إنه» ترجع إلى الأمر والشأن. ويجوز إن من يأت،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r12.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r12.claim: The cited line about one who enters a church illustrates the implied affair construction.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r12.anchor:
ومنه قول الشاعر:
إن من يدخل الكنيسة يوما
يلق فيها جآذرا وظباء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r13.claim: مجرم can mean disbeliever or sinner; the disbeliever sense better fits the description of Hell and is explained at 4:56.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r13.anchor: والمجرم الكافر. وقيل: الذي يقترف المعاصي ويكتسبها. والأول أشبه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r14.claim: The condemned person's life brings no benefit and death brings no relief.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r14.anchor: فلا ينتفع بحياته ولا يستريح بموته

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r15.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r15.claim: Another explanation says the unbeliever's soul remains caught in his throat: it neither leaves so he dies nor settles so he truly lives.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r15.anchor: وقيل: نفس الكافر معلقة في حنجرته كما أخبر الله تعالى عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r16.claim: To come to one's Lord as a criminal means to come to one's Lord's appointed meeting.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r16.anchor: ومعنى { من يأت ربه مجرما } من يأت موعد ربه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r17.claim: To come to Him as a believer means to die and arrive affirming Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r17.anchor: ومعنى { ومن يأته مؤمنا } أي يمت عليه ويوافيه مصدقا به.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r18.claim: The good deeds are acts of obedience and doing what was commanded while avoiding what was prohibited.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r18.anchor: { قد عمل } أي وقد عمل { الصالحات } أي الطاعات وما أمر به ونهي عنه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r19.claim: The elevated degrees are exalted ranks beyond which descriptions cannot reach.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r19.anchor: أي الرفيعة التي قصرت دونها الصفات

QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r20.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r20.claim: The contrast with the believer shows that مجرم here means the polytheist.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:73-76/r20.anchor: ودل قوله: { ومن يأته مؤمنا } على أن المراد بالمجرم المشرك

QASHANI:20:74-78/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:74-78/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:74-78/r1.claim: In the minor resurrection, a criminal arrives burdened by bodily dispositions that incline toward natural bodies; he neither dies a natural death and feels no pain nor lives truly to escape sin's consequences.
QASHANI:20:74-78/r1.anchor: في القيامة الصغرى مجرما مثقلا بالهيئات البدنية المميلة إلى الأجرام الطبيعية

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r1.claim: The hāʾ in innahu is the pronoun of the matter: the matter is as follows.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r1.anchor: ضمير الشأن يعني أن الأمر والشأن كذا وكذا

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r2.claim: The Muʿtazila infer a definitive threat for major sinners: every major sinner is a criminal, and the conditional man is general because any individual may be excepted.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r2.anchor: استدلت المعتزلة بهذه الآية في القطع على وعيد أصحاب الكبائر

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r3.speaker: بعض المتكلمين من أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r3.claim: Some of al-Rāzī’s fellow theologians deny that a major sinner is called a criminal, since the passage contrasts the criminal with the believer; they also cite 83:29.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r3.anchor: واعترض بعض المتكلمين من أصحابنا على هذا الكلام

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r4.speaker: بعض المتكلمين من أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r4.claim: The objectors add that a major sinner, even if punished in the Fire, does not remain in the condition of neither dying nor living described here.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r4.anchor: والمؤمن صاحب الكبيرة وإن عذب بالنار لا يكون بهذا الوصف

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r5.claim: The objection cites a report graded sound: whoever has a particle’s weight of faith in his heart will leave the Fire.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r5.anchor: وفي الخبر الصحيح : ( يخرج من النار من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من الإيمان )

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r6.claim: The contrast with believers only answers the Muʿtazila if major sinners are believers, which their own doctrine denies; the objection assumes its proponents’ position.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r6.anchor: هذا إنما ينفع لو ثبت أن صاحب الكبيرة مؤمن

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r7.claim: The description does not exclude a major sinner, because Hell’s punishment is extremely severe; al-Rāzī cites 3:192.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r7.anchor: لا نسلم فإن عذاب جهنم في غاية الشدة

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r8.claim: One proposed answer is that the Qurʾān is mass-transmitted and cannot be opposed by a solitary report.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r8.anchor: القرآن متواتر فلا يعارضه خبر الواحد

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r9.speaker: الخصم
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r9.claim: A counterargument allows a solitary report to specify the Qurʾān in practical rulings, but says its probabilistic force cannot settle a matter of belief.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r9.anchor: يجوز تخصيص القرآن بخبر الواحد وللخصم أن يجيب فيقول ذلك يفيد الظن

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r10.speaker: معترض آخر
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r10.claim: Another objector says the threat is agreed to be conditional on absence of repentance and of reward that cancels punishment; those without divine pardon must enter Hell.

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r11.claim: No separate repentance condition is needed: the verse describes someone arriving before God as a criminal, which does not describe a repentant person.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r11.anchor: أما شرط نفي التوبة فلا حاجة إليه

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r12.claim: A minor sinner is not called a criminal, since mujrim is a term of blame and should not be applied to someone who commits a minor sin.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r12.anchor: وأما صاحب الصغيرة فلأنه لا يسمى مجرما لأن المجرم اسم للذم

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r13.claim: The sound objection is that the general threat conflicts with the following general promise for a believer who did righteous deeds and later committed a major sin.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r13.anchor: الاعتراض الصحيح أن نقول : عموم هذا الوعيد معارض بما جاء بعده من عموم الوعد

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r14.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r14.claim: The Muʿtazila say the sin’s punishment cancels the reward of prior obedience, so the promise does not rescue the major sinner.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r14.anchor: فإن قيل : عقاب المعصية يحبط ثواب الطاعة

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r15.claim: Al-Rāzī counters that the reward of faith may instead repel the punishment for sin.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r15.anchor: قلنا : لم لا يجوز أن يقال : ثواب الإيمان يدفع عقاب المعصية

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r16.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r16.claim: The Muʿtazila object that if faith’s reward offset sin, the major sinner should neither be cursed nor subjected to a legal penalty.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r16.anchor: لو كان كذلك لوجب أن لا يجوز لعنه وإقامة الحد عليه

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r17.claim: Al-Rāzī says cursing such a person is impermissible, while a legal penalty may serve as a trial, as with a repentant person, or as deterrence.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r17.anchor: وأما إقامة الحد عليه فقد تكون على سبيل المحنة كما في حق التائب

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r18.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r18.claim: Citing 5:38, the Muʿtazila argue that a penalty imposed as deterrence precludes deserving praise and honor, and therefore eliminates reward.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r18.anchor: قالت المعتزلة قوله تعالى : { والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r19.claim: Al-Rāzī says the deterrent-penalty text conflicts with texts granting reward, with no basis to privilege either: believers include thieves and non-thieves, and thieves include believers and unbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r19.anchor: النص الدال على إقامة الحد عليه على سبيل التنكيل صار معارضا

RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r20.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r20.claim: The generality of man is only probabilistic, whereas this doctrinal issue requires certainty; al-Rāzī refers readers to al-Maḥṣūl for the full argument.
RAZI-FULL:v22p78/r20.anchor: لا نسلم أن كلمة من في إفادة العموم قطعية بل ظنية ومسألتنا قطعية

RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r1.speaker: المجسمة
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r1.claim: The corporealists argue that a body could come to its Lord only if the Lord occupied a place.
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r1.anchor: تمسكت المجسمة بقوله : { إنه من يأت ربه مجرما }

RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī answers that coming to God means metaphorically coming to the place of the promised reward, as Abraham said he was going to his Lord (37:99).
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r2.anchor: جعل إتيانهم موضع الوعد إتيانا إلى الله مجازا

RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r3.claim: Since a living body must be either alive or dead, the verse means the person suffers Hell’s worst state: no relieving death and no enjoyable life.
RAZI-FULL:v22p79/r3.anchor: فمعناه في الآية أنه يكون في جهنم بأسوء حال لا يموت موتة مريحة ولا يحيا حياة ممتعة

STUDYQURAN:20:74/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:74/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:74/r1.claim: Hell's inhabitants neither die nor live because they have no rest and no life from which they can draw positive benefit.
STUDYQURAN:20:74/r1.anchor: One neither dies nor lives in Hell because its inhabitants will not experience rest in it, nor will they live a kind of life from which they can draw positive benefit

TABATABAI:20:74-75/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r4.claim: The warning about Gehenna explains why they make forgiveness the goal of faith: one whose sins are not forgiven remains a criminal.
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r4.anchor: تعليل لجعل غفران الخطايا غاية للإيمان بالله أي لأن من لم يغفر خطاياه كان مجرما

TABATABAI:20:74-75/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r5.claim: Unlike worldly punishment, the criminal in Hell cannot escape torment through death, yet has none of the good or hope that makes life pleasant.
TABATABAI:20:74-75/r5.anchor: لا يموت فيها حتى ينجو من مقاساة ألم عذابها لكن منتهى عذاب الدنيا الموت

TABRISI:20:74-76/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:74-76/r2.speaker: ابن عباس عن الضحاك
TABRISI:20:74-76/r2.claim: In a report from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn ʿAbbās explains mujrim as a disbeliever.
TABRISI:20:74-76/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: في رواية الضحاك المجرم الكافر

TABRISI:20:74-76/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:74-76/r3.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
TABRISI:20:74-76/r3.claim: In a report from ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn ʿAbbās says it means someone who committed wrongdoing like Pharaoh's.
TABRISI:20:74-76/r3.anchor: وفي رواية عطاء يعني الذي أجرم وفعل مثل ما فعل فرعون

TABRISI:20:74-76/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:74-76/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:74-76/r4.claim: The condemned person does not die and escape punishment, nor live with relief; instead he suffers many kinds of torment.
TABRISI:20:74-76/r4.anchor: فيستريح من العذاب { ولا يحيى } حياة فيها راحة بل هو معاقب بأنواع العقاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r1.claim: The author treats this as God’s own speech beginning here, so the sorcerers’ quoted speech ends before this verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r1.anchor: هذا ابتداء كلام من الله تعالى وانتهى الإخبار عن السحرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r2.speaker: آخرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r2.claim: Another view says the verse remains part of what the sorcerers said.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r2.anchor: وقيل: (هذا أيضا إخبار عنهم أنهم قالوه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r3.claim: The pronoun in innahu may refer to the matter or affair, or be a pronoun awaiting explanation; the author points to the same construction in 12:90.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r3.anchor: والكناية في قوله: {إنه} الأمر والشأن، أي: بأن الأمر والشأن هذا، وهو أن المجرم يدخل النار، والمؤمن يدخل الجنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, in the report through al-Dahhak, glosses mujrim as an unbeliever.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية الضحاك: (المجرم الكافر)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r5.claim: In the report through ʿAta, Ibn Abbas says the term means committing the same wrongdoing as Pharaoh.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية الضحاك: (المجرم الكافر) (¬2). وقال في رواية عطاء: (يريد أجرم، وفعل مثل ما فعل فرعون)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r6.claim: The damned neither die and find relief nor live in a way that lifts the punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r6.anchor: قال: (يريد لا يموت فيستريح، ولا يحيي فيفتر عنه العذاب)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r7.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi says they do not have a life in Hell that benefits them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r7.anchor: قال الكلبي: (ولا يحيي فيها حياة تنفعه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r8.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r8.claim: Abu Nadr transmits from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri that the Prophet said those whom God will not remove from Hell are killed by the Fire until charcoal, then brought in groups to Paradise’s rivers and revived by their water like seeds in flood silt; no grading is given.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r8.anchor: وروى أبو نضرة (¬1) عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: "إن أهل النار الذين لا يريد الله إخراجهم تميتهم النار إماتة حتى يصيروا فحما، ثم يخرجون ضبائر (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r9.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r9.claim: Al-Mubarrad says this means no restful death and no enjoyable life: they still feel pain, but their condition is like the dead in misery; Arabic likewise says someone is neither living nor dead when life benefits nothing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r9.anchor: قال المبرد: (تأويل قوله: {لا يموت فيها ولا يحيى} لا يموت ميتة مريحة، ولا يحيى حياة ممتعة، وهو يألم كما يألم الحي ليفهم ذلك،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r10.speaker: ابن مرداس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r10.claim: Ibn Mirdas’s line about receiving nothing and being denied nothing illustrates a state in which an apparent outcome falls short of its purpose.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r10.anchor:
كما قال ابن مرداس (¬2) (¬3):
وقد كنت في الحرب ذا تدراء ... فلم أعط شيئا ولم أمنع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r11.speaker: عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة بن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r11.claim: The cited verse by ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUtba describes a soul that neither dies to end its misery nor lives a life with any taste.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p467/r11.anchor:
وأنشد ابن الأنباري في مثل هذا المعنى لعبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة بن مسعود (¬4):
ألا ما لنفس لا تموت فينقضي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:74-76/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:74-76/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:74-76/r1.claim: The criminal dies in associationism; in Hell he neither dies for relief nor lives a beneficial life.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:74-76/r1.anchor: { إنه من يأت ربه مجرما } مات على الشرك { فإن له جهنم لا يموت فيها } فيستريح بالموت { ولا يحيا } حياة تنفعه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p267/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p267/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p267/r4.anchor: قوله: {إنه من يأت ربه مجرما} [طه: 74] مشركا.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237#2/r1.claim: تطلع على الأفئدة means that the Fire rises over or looms above the hearts, like someone who climbs a mountain and overlooks it.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237#2/r1.anchor: قوله: تطلع على الأفئدة أي توفي عليها وتشرف،

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237#2/r2.claim: The hearts are singled out because pain reaching the heart kills; the damned endure a deathlike condition without actually dying, as in the verse about Hell.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237#2/r2.anchor: وخص الأفئدة، لأن الألم إذا صار إلى الفؤاد مات صاحبه.

NAHHAS:v3p49/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p49/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p49/r9.claim: The pronoun in إنه is a pronoun of the matter, and the following sentence is the predicate of إن.
NAHHAS:v3p49/r9.anchor: الهاء كناية عن الحديث والجملة خبر إن

TABRISI:20:71-74/r25.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:71-74/r25.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:71-74/r25.claim: At this point the account of the magicians ends and the discourse shifts to the next statement about whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal.
TABRISI:20:71-74/r25.anchor: وههنا انتهى الإخبار عن السحرة. ثم قال الله سبحانه { إنه من يأت ربه مجرما }

THALABI:v6p253/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p253/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p253/r13.claim: A criminal here is one who dies persisting in polytheism; Hell gives him neither death and relief nor a life that benefits him.
THALABI:v6p253/r13.anchor: يعني بات على الشرك فإن له جهنم لا يموت فيها فيستريح ولا يحيى حياة تنفعه

BURHAN:v4p29/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p29/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p29/r7.claim: The opening pronoun remains masculine although the clause mentions feminine Jahannam, because the intended sense is that a guilty arrival is punished with Hell.
BURHAN:v4p29/r7.anchor: فذكر الضمير مع اشتمال الجملة على جهنم وهي مؤنثة

BURHAN:v2p279/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p279/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p279/r11.claim: A person who comes to his Lord as a criminal is named by the criminal state he had in worldly life.
BURHAN:v2p279/r11.anchor: سماه مجرما باعتبار ما كان عليه في الدنيا من الاجرام

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهالأسماءالتييجاز.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهالأسماءالتييجاز.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماتكونفيهالأسماءالتييجاز.claim: The verse إنه من يأت ربه مجرما فإن له جهنم shows a conditional clause after إنه, whose explicit pronoun leaves room for the conditional.
